sections.h2: Where is Douglas County, Colorado, and what is it like?
sections.html:
Douglas County sits south of Denver, with Castle Rock as its county seat, and it covers roughly 843 square miles.

It was one of the original 17 counties of the Colorado Territory, created on November 1, 1861 and named for U.S. Senator Stephen A. Douglas of Illinois. The seat moved from Franktown to California Ranch in 1863 and to Castle Rock in 1874. That same year most of the eastern part of the county went to Elbert County.

The 2020 census counted 357,978 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 399,396. Highlands Ranch is the largest community. Parker, Lone Tree, Castle Pines and Castle Rock are other places you will see on tax bills, and Littleton and Aurora each reach partly into the county.

sections.h2: What does the land look like, and why does it matter for a house?
sections.html:
The county has mesas, foothills, small streams and ponderosa pine, and that terrain affects flood zones, wildfire exposure and lot values.

Cherry Creek and Plum Creek both rise here and run north toward Denver, and both are now dammed. Plum Creek flash flooding was partly blamed for the 1965 Denver flood. Part of the county lies in Pike National Forest, and three state parks are inside its borders:

  • Castlewood Canyon
  • Chatfield
  • Roxborough

Rueter-Hess Reservoir is the largest body of water. If your lot backs onto open space, a creek or a forested slope, a buyer's insurance quote can shape the offer, and a cash buyer can skip that wait.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers and school district in Douglas County?
sections.html:
Douglas County School District RE-1 covers the whole county, is the third-largest district in Colorado, and was the county's biggest employer in a 2015 report.

That report listed these employers, so treat the headcounts as dated:

Douglas County School District RE-15,563

Many residents also commute toward Denver and the south metro job centers. Sellers who relocate for work often need to close on a set date, which is where a short cash timeline helps.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Douglas County?
sections.html:
The Douglas County Assessor values property and the Treasurer collects the tax.

The Assessor's office is at 301 Wilcox Street in Castle Rock, open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The phone is 303-660-7450, and the county main line is 303-660-7400.

The Treasurer's page offers an interactive "Where do my taxes go?" map. It shows the taxing authorities and total mill levy for your property's district designation. Because the total depends on the district designation, two nearby houses can carry different totals.

sections.h2: What are the 2026 valuation and appeal dates in Douglas County?
sections.html:
For 2026, the Assessor released notices of value on May 1, and written objections were due June 8.

2026 dateEvent
May 1Real property Notices of Value released, appeals begin
June 8Deadline for written objections by mail or online
June 15Business personal property appeals open
June 30Business personal property appeals must be delivered or postmarked

This settles a question raised by older county pages that mentioned both June 1 and June 8. The county's 2026 notice gives June 8 for homeowners. In-person meetings can be scheduled online.

Only properties with a change in value, use or ownership get a notice, which the county says is fewer than 10% of owners. If you did not get one, your value probably carried forward.

sections.h2: How are Douglas County homes valued under Colorado rules?
sections.html:
Colorado values homes on comparable sales, then applies an assessment rate and the local mill levy.

The state calls the steps classification, actual value, assessed value and tax rate. Residential has used two assessment rates since 2025: one for local governments and one for schools. The state's 2026 chart shows 6.8% and 7.05%. Comparable sales for tax years 2025 and 2026 come from January 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024, with earlier periods used if data is thin.

The state's worked example uses a $275,000 home and totals $1,448.48. Your own number will differ with your levy. Revenue stays in the county and supports schools, counties, special districts, municipalities and junior colleges.

sections.h2: What happens after a Douglas County appeal is denied?
sections.html:
You can keep going. Under the state's process, the next stop after the Assessor is the county Board of Equalization, and it must give you its decision in writing within five business days.

If you still disagree, you have 30 days from the mailed decision to go to an arbitrator, district court or the state Board of Assessment Appeals.

State schedule stepStandardAlternate
Appeal to AssessorJune 8June 8
Notice of Determination mailedLast working day in JuneAugust 15
Board of Equalization hearings beginJuly 1September 1
Board of Equalization responds byAugust 5November 1

The state says counties over 300,000 residents must use the alternate schedule. Douglas County had 357,978 residents in 2020, so confirm with the Assessor which column applies to your notice.

sections.h2: Are there tax relief programs for Douglas County homeowners?
sections.html:
Yes, Colorado lists several statewide programs that Douglas County owners can ask about.

  • Property tax, rent and heat rebate
  • Property tax deferral
  • Work-off program
  • Senior property tax exemption
  • Veteran with a disability exemption

The state Division of Property Taxation can be reached at (303) 864-7777. Applications and deadlines are set by the state, so ask before you list. A seller who qualifies may owe less than the bill suggests.

sections.h2: What happens if Douglas County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes can be sold as a tax lien. The 2026 internet tax lien sale in Douglas County is set for November 5, 2026, with an interest rate of 13%.

The Treasurer explains that the rate is nine points above the federal discount rate as of September 1. The buyer gets a lien, not the property, and a deed transfer happens in less than 1 percent of purchases.

  • The county listing we reviewed says delinquent notices are mailed in July
  • The lien sale is the last step for most accounts
  • A lien investor collects interest from the owner
  • Paying before the sale avoids that interest

If you are behind and thinking of selling, the clock matters. Tax debt grows while you wait for a traditional listing to find a buyer.

sections.h2: How do I handle Douglas County property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Order a current balance, confirm which half-year payments are made, and let the closing agent pay what is owed from your proceeds.

  • Pay first half by the end of February and second half by June 15, or the full amount by April 30
  • Keep your statement and payment receipts for both halves
  • Check Notices of Value each May, because a protest affects the next bill
  • Ask about senior and veteran exemptions if they apply to you

A tax-delinquent house, an inherited house or a rental with a code problem is exactly what many sellers here bring to a cash buyer.

faqs.q: What is the Douglas County property tax appeal deadline in 2026?
faqs.a: June 8, 2026 for real property objections, by mail or online. Notices of Value were released May 1.

faqs.q: Where is the Douglas County Assessor's office?
faqs.a: 301 Wilcox Street, Castle Rock. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The phone is 303-660-7450.

faqs.q: When is the 2026 Douglas County tax lien sale?
faqs.a: November 5, 2026, held online. The 2026 interest rate is 13%.

faqs.q: Is Castle Rock the county seat?
faqs.a: Yes. The seat moved there from California Ranch in 1874, after starting out in Franktown. Today the Assessor and the county offices sit on Wilcox Street in Castle Rock.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Douglas County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid at closing from the proceeds. Get a current payoff from the Treasurer before you accept an offer.
